rationale: C10 plausibly supplied a concrete and material template. It asks Congress to establish a commission concerning the Executive Mansion, specifies the commission's role in addressing renovation and modernization, invokes prior congressional commission practice, and urges prompt enactment. The child adapts that same legislative-commission mechanism to the closely related problem of Presidential office space and expressly identifies the earlier Executive Mansion commission as complementary. C22 and C02 share study-and-recommendation commission machinery, but their targets and establishment by executive order make them less direct models.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am submitting herewith for consideration of the Congress a draft bill "To provide for the establishment of a President's Advisory Commission on Presidential Office Space."
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I consider it appropriate that the Congress should establish a Commission
shared_material.explanation: Both letters ask Congress to create a presidential-facilities commission through legislation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This Commission will, in effect, complement the work of the earlier Commission for the Renovation of the Executive Mansion
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a Commission which would exercise general supervision and direction of all construction work involved in the renovation and modernization of the mansion
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly positions its proposed body as a successor or complement to the commission proposed in C10.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I strongly urge that this proposed legislation be acted upon before the close of the present session of Congress.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I trust, therefore, that at the earliest possible date the Congress will enact legislation to establish a commission
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude by urging expedited congressional establishment of the commission.
